Robert Oppenheimer) and the subsequent director (Norris Bradbury). The error stems from a misinterpretation of historical roles; Oppenheimer was the director of the Los Alamos Laboratory (Project Y) during the development of the first atomic bomb (Trinity test in 1945), whereas Bradbury took over leadership later. By prematurely concluding Bradbury was the answer based on incomplete verification of Oppenheimer's specific role in the *first* bomb's development, the Planner set the conversation on an incorrect path, leading to redundant searches and a wrong final answer.
